answers.docs.gaps:
Nothing in `docs/` was wrong. Everything I relied on behaved as documented,
including the two subtle ones I leaned on hardest:

> "`NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` suppress the capability, so they turn `auto`
> plain" and "A `term` request is unconditional, and the environment's color
> conventions do not override it" — docs/topics/output-modes.md

`NO_COLOR=1 systemdlike --output term` did emit ANSI, and
`SYSTEMDLIKE_COLORS=1 systemdlike --output text` did not.

> "a refused line is offered to it — `myapp --all` is a naked line at a root
> that has no `--all`, and becomes `myapp list --all`"
> — docs/topics/app-configuration.md

`systemdlike --no-legend --state active` behaved as `systemdlike list-units
--no-legend --state active`, byte for byte.

Two gaps rather than errors:

- No page documents how an application pages its own command output, or what a
  `run_with` caller should re-implement to match `run()`'s final write. The
  ingredients are all in docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md, but they are
  described as what `run()` does, not as a recipe for replacing it.
- `TargetProperties` has no reference page of its own. Its fields appear only
  inside a struct literal in an example
  (docs/crates/render/guides/intro-to-rendering.md) and as facts a test harness
  injects (docs/topics/testing.md). Writing `target.stdout_color_capability`
  and reading `target.stdout_is_terminal` at the process edge is the natural
  way to implement the spec's colour and pager rules, and it works, but nothing
  states that these fields are a supported adopter seam rather than an
  incidental detail of the example.
answers.friction:
The pager is the one real gap between the spec and the framework. Everything I
could find about paging is about help topics:

> "The one exception is a paged help display (`SuccessKind::PagedHelp`), which
> goes to the pager instead" — docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md

> "For long topics, the `--page` flag displays content through a pager"
> — docs/topics/topics-system.md

There is no equivalent for a command's own output, and `standout-pipe`'s
`pipe_through`/`pipe_to` are the wrong shape for it: they are unconditional per
command, they run whether or not stdout is attended, and
docs/crates/pipe/topics/piping.md says "Piped content is always plain text …
all ANSI escape codes stripped automatically", which would defeat the colour
rules. So the spec's pager discipline forced me off `app.run(...)` and onto
`app.run_with(...)` plus a hand-written final write. That is a documented,
supported path — but it means re-implementing the framework's own emission
rules (stdout, `writeln!`, BrokenPipe-is-success, usage-error exit 2), which
the docs describe well enough to copy but do not expose as a reusable helper.

Related, and the one thing that actually cost me a fix: `run_with` returns the
same text for a command page and for clap's `--version` display, but the two
have different newline conventions.

    $ systemdlike --version | od -c
    0000000  s y s t e m d l i k e   0 . 1 . 0  \n  \n

The command page never ends in a newline (the engine eats the last one), so
`writeln!` is right for it — that is the documented contract:

> "`App::run` writes a handled command's text with `writeln!`, so what reaches
> stdout is the rendered string plus one `\n`" — docs/crates/render/topics/
> templating.md

but clap's version string already carries its own `\n`, and the docs do not say
that `run()` treats the two differently. `emit()` now branches on
`SuccessKind::Command` to normalize it.

Smaller: `tabular()`/`table()` cannot size a column from the table's content,
so they do not fit this spec's layout rule at all —

> "A `{"min": ..., "max": ...}` column is resolved once, when `tabular()` or
> `table()` builds the formatter, before any row is seen — it does not measure
> row content. … Resolving a top-level column's width from every row's content
> … is issue #359" — docs/crates/render/guides/intro-to-tabular.md

which sent me to the `col` filter with widths computed in the view instead.
The doc is explicit about the limitation, so this cost reading time, not
debugging time.

answers.summary:
`systemdlike`, complete and working, in `app/`. `cargo build`, `cargo clippy
--all-targets` and `cargo test` are all clean (7 tests pass).

Layout:
- `src/units.rs` — the frozen unit table and `list_units(Option<ActiveState>)`.
  CLI-free: no clap, no printing, no output concerns. Two unit tests pin the
  listing order and the `--state` filter.
- `src/view.rs` — `UnitListView`, the serializable view data. It holds the
  rows, the count, whether the legend is shown, and the column widths measured
  over the rows that will actually be rendered (header row included only when
  it is shown).
- `src/templates/list-units.jinja` — the whole layout: header row, data rows,
  blank line, `<N> units listed.`. Columns are joined with a single space and
  padded with the `col` filter; the last column (`SUB`) is never padded.
- `src/styles/default.css` — `.header` bold, `.active` green, `.inactive` red,
  `.legend` gray.
- `src/main.rs` — clap `Cli`, `#[derive(Subcommand, Dispatch)]` with
  `#[dispatch(pure, default)] ListUnits`, the `#[handler]` adapter, and the
  process edge (colour discipline, pager discipline, exit codes).

How the spec's rules map onto the framework:

- Naked invocation: `#[dispatch(default)]` on `ListUnits`. `systemdlike
  --no-legend` is refused by the root, the default is substituted, and
  `list-units --no-legend` parses — exactly as `topics/app-configuration.md`
  describes. Verified byte-identical to the explicit spelling.
- Colour: the four rules resolve to one fact the framework reads for
  `--output auto`, `TargetProperties::stdout_color_capability`. `main` calls
  `TargetProperties::detect()` and then overrides that field per rules 1–3
  (`--plain`, `SYSTEMDLIKE_COLORS`, `NO_COLOR`), leaving rule 4 alone when none
  applies. The `--output` half of rule 1 needs no code: per
  `topics/output-modes.md`, an explicit `term`/`text` request is unconditional
  and the environment never reaches it.
- Paging: standout has no pager for command output (only `help --page`), so
  `main` uses `run_with` to capture the rendered page and performs the final
  write itself — through `sh -c $SYSTEMDLIKE_PAGER` (else `$PAGER`) when
  stdout is attended, `--no-pager` was not given, and the outcome is
  `SuccessKind::Command`; to stdout otherwise. If the pager fails to spawn the
  page still goes to stdout.
- Exit codes: `RunErrorKind::ClapUsage` → 2, other run errors → 1, success → 0.
  `--state` uses a clap `value_parser`, so a bad value is a usage error for
  free.

Verified by running the binary: default, `list-units`, `--state
active|inactive`, `--no-legend`, `--plain`, and the naked-vs-explicit
equivalences all match the spec byte for byte (`diff` against the spec's own
fenced blocks). Exit codes checked for unknown subcommand, unknown flag on both
the naked and explicit lines, bad `--state`, `--help`, `--version`, and
`--output=nonsense`. Colour checked over the full rule matrix on a pipe,
including `SYSTEMDLIKE_COLORS=1 NO_COLOR=1` (ANSI) and `SYSTEMDLIKE_COLORS=1
--plain` (plain); stripping the ANSI from the styled output reproduces the
plain output exactly.
answers.workarounds:
Three, all in `src/main.rs`:

- `--plain` and `--no-pager` are declared on `list-units` for clap to validate
  and document, but `run()` also scans raw `argv` for them, because both
  decisions belong to the process edge and are needed before and after
  `run_with` rather than inside the handler. The scan is a plain string
  comparison; a value-carrying spelling would not match, but neither flag takes
  a value.
- `run()` re-implements standout's final write (`writeln!` to stdout,
  BrokenPipe treated as success, usage errors to stderr with status 2) instead
  of calling `app.run(...)`, because `run()` owns the write and there is no
  seam for paging a command's output. If the framework ever grows one, this
  whole block collapses back to `app.run(...)`.
- `--plain` is implemented as a colour-capability override, which the framework
  reads only for `--output auto`. So `--plain --output term` still emits ANSI.
  SPEC.md puts both in rule 1 without saying which wins, so this combination is
  undefined either way; every case rule 1 does name ("regardless of terminal,
  color variables, or theme") is covered.

One deliberate non-workaround worth flagging: `UnitListView` carries `widths`
and `show_legend`, so those appear in `--output json`/`yaml`/`csv` alongside
the units. SPEC.md does not define the structured modes. I kept the layout
facts in the view rather than branching on output mode in the handler, which
docs/topics/output-modes.md ("Keep Output Mode Out of Handlers") asks for.
